full_text_en:
**Industrial and Commercial Bank of China Limited, Sanmenxia Station Sub-branch v. Sanmenxia Tianyuan Aluminum Co., Ltd. and Sanmenxia Tianyuan Aluminum Group Co., Ltd. — Dispute Over Loan Guarantee Contract**

**Ruling Summary**

I. Pursuant to the provisions of Article 84 of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China, a debtor's transfer of all or part of its contractual obligations to a third party shall be subject to the consent of the creditor. Therefore, where the debtor issues a letter of undertaking to the creditor indicating an intention to transfer all or part of its debts to a third party, but the creditor does not accept such transfer and does not affix its official seal to the debt transfer agreement executed between the debtor and the third party, it shall be determined that the creditor does not consent to the debt transfer, and the debt transfer agreement between the debtor and the third party shall have no legal effect against the creditor.

II. The practice of "repaying old loans with new loans" occurs when, upon the inability to recover a loan upon maturity, the creditor (a financial institution) enters into an agreement with the debtor to extend a new loan to the debtor for the purpose of repaying the existing loan. This practice is fundamentally different from the situation where a debtor uses its own funds to repay a loan, thereby extinguishing the original creditor-debtor relationship. Although the new loan replaces the old loan, the original creditor-debtor relationship is not eliminated; objectively, the new loan merely extends the repayment period of the old loan.

**Civil Judgment of the Supreme People's Court**
No. 81 (2008) Min Er Zhong Zi

Appellant (Plaintiff at First Instance): Industrial and Commercial Bank of China Limited, Sanmenxia Station Sub-branch, domiciled at No. 7 Middle Xiaoshan Road, Sanmenxia City, Henan Province.
Person in Charge: Dong Chaoqun, Branch Manager.
Authorized Agent: Chai Yi, Staff Member, Industrial and Commercial Bank of China, Sanmenxia Branch.
Authorized Agent: Xu Xinhai, Attorney at Law, Beijing Far East Law Firm.

Appellee (Defendant at First Instance): Sanmenxia Tianyuan Aluminum Co., Ltd., domiciled at No. 10 South Dongfeng Road, Sanmenxia City, Henan Province.
Legal Representative: Li Heping, Chairman of the Board.
Authorized Agent: Song Dongmin, Staff Member of the Company.
Authorized Agent: Guo Yaping, Attorney at Law, Beijing Branch of Henan Century Tong Law Firm.

Defendant at First Instance: Sanmenxia Tianyuan Aluminum Group Co., Ltd., domiciled at No. 10 South Dongfeng Road, Sanmenxia City, Henan Province.
Legal Representative: Zhu Qiang, Chairman of the Board.

The Appellant, Industrial and Commercial Bank of China Limited, Sanmenxia Station Sub-branch (hereinafter referred to as Sanmenxia Station ICBC), appealed to this Court against the Civil Judgment No. 44 (2006) Yu Fa Min Er Chu Zi rendered by the Henan High People's Court in the case of a dispute over a loan guarantee contract with the Appellee, Sanmenxia Tianyuan Aluminum Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Tianyuan Stock Company), the Defendant at First Instance, Sanmenxia Tianyuan Aluminum Group Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Tianyuan Group Company), and the former Sanmenxia Tiancheng Electrochemical Co., Ltd. (bankruptcy concluded, hereinafter referred to as Tiancheng Electrochemical Company). This Court lawfully formed a collegial panel composed of Presiding Judge Zhang Shuming, Acting Judges Wang Huaju and Sha Ling to conduct the trial. The court record was kept by Clerk Zhao Suijun. This case has now been concluded.

The court of first instance found the following facts:

On September 22, 2000, Sanmenxia Station ICBC and Tianyuan Group Company executed Loan Contract No. (2000) San Gong Che Xin Zi No. 010, which provided that Tianyuan Group Company would borrow RMB 17,000,000 from Sanmenxia Station ICBC, with the purpose of the loan being "repaying old loans with new loans," and the loan term from the date of signing to September 21, 2002. On the same day, Sanmenxia Station ICBC disbursed the loan to Tianyuan Group Company. On September 11, 2002, Tianyuan Group Company repaid this loan. The next day, the two parties executed Loan Contracts No. (2002) San Gong Che Xin Zi No. 039-1 and No. 039-2, providing respectively that Tianyuan Group Company would borrow RMB 9,000,000 and RMB 8,000,000 from Sanmenxia Station ICBC, with the purpose of both loans being "repaying old loans with new loans," and the loan term from the date of signing to September 5, 2003. Sanmenxia Station ICBC disbursed these two loans on the date of signing. On September 3, 2003, Tianyuan Group Company repaid these two loans totaling RMB 17,000,000. On September 5, 2003, the two parties executed Loan Contract No. (2003) San Gong Che Xin Zi No. 039, providing that Tianyuan Group Company would borrow RMB 16,000,000 from Sanmenxia Station ICBC, with the purpose being "purchase of raw materials," and the loan term from the date of signing to August 25, 2004. Sanmenxia Station ICBC disbursed this loan on the date of signing. On August 3, 2004, Tianyuan Group Company repaid this loan. On August 5, 2004, the two parties executed Loan Contract No. (2004) San Gong Che Xin Zi No. 37, providing that Tianyuan Group Company would borrow RMB 15,900,000 from Sanmenxia Station ICBC, with the purpose being "purchase of raw materials," and the loan term from the date of signing to August 3, 2005.

On September 25, 2000, the two parties executed Loan Contract No. (2000) San Gong Che Xin Zi No. 009, providing that Tianyuan Group Company would borrow RMB 16,470,000 from Sanmenxia Station ICBC, with the purpose of the loan being "repaying old loans with new loans," and the loan term from the date of signing to September 24, 2002. Sanmenxia Station ICBC disbursed the loan on the date of signing. On September 11, 2002, the two parties executed Loan Contracts No. (2002) San Gong Che Xin Zi No. 038-1 and No. (2002) San Gong Che Xin Zi No. 038-2, providing respectively that Tianyuan Group Company would borrow RMB 12,000,000 and RMB 8,000,000 from Sanmenxia Station ICBC, with the purpose of both loans being "repay old loans and borrow new loans, purchase raw materials," and the loan term from the date of signing to September 10, 2003. Sanmenxia Station ICBC disbursed these two loans on the date of signing. The day after receiving the RMB 20,000,000 loan, Tianyuan Group Company repaid the RMB 16,470,000 loan under Loan Contract No. (2000) San Gong Che Xin Zi No. 009. Tianyuan Group Company repaid RMB 2,200,000 to Sanmenxia Station ICBC on August 4, 2003, and repaid RMB 12,000,000 and RMB 8,000,000 on September 8, 2003. On August 7, 2003, the two parties executed Loan Contract No. (2003) San Gong Che Xin Zi No. 35, providing that Tianyuan Group Company would borrow RMB 7,100,000 from Sanmenxia Station ICBC, with the purpose being "purchase of raw materials," and the loan term from the date of signing to August 6, 2004. On August 29, 2003, the two parties executed Loan Contract No. (2003) San Gong Che Xin Zi No. 38, providing that Tianyuan Group Company would borrow RMB 14,900,000 from Sanmenxia Station ICBC, with the purpose being "purchase of raw materials," and the loan term from the date of signing to August 29, 2004. Both loans were disbursed on the date of signing. Tianyuan Group Company repaid each of these two loans on August 5, 2004. On August 6, 2004, Sanmenxia Station ICBC and Tianyuan Group Company executed Loan Contracts No. (2004) San Gong Che Xin Zi No. 38 and No. 39, providing respectively that Tianyuan Group Company would borrow RMB 14,800,000 and RMB 7,000,000 from Sanmenxia Station ICBC. These two loans matured on August 5, 2005.

The above three loans were all guaranteed by Tiancheng Electrochemical Company on a joint and several liability basis.

The court of first instance also found: Tianyuan Stock Company was established in August 2000 as a joint stock limited company by five corporate shareholders: Tianyuan Group Company, Baiyin Fluoride Salt Co., Ltd., Jiaozuo Cryolite Factory, Henan No. 6 Construction Engineering Company, and Jiaozuo Jiao Lv Carbon Factory, with registered capital of RMB 68,000,000. Tianyuan Group Company contributed RMB 65,176,184, representing 95.84% of the total shares. Asia Pacific Evaluation Firm conducted an asset evaluation of Tianyuan Group Company as of November 30, 1999, concluding that the net assets of Tianyuan Group Company were RMB 92,326,000. On September 21, 2000, Tianyuan Group Company issued a letter of undertaking to Sanmenxia Station ICBC stating: Tianyuan Group Company would contribute its existing high-quality assets (Electrolysis No. 1 Plant, Electrolysis No. 2 Plant, power workshop, and other auxiliary workshops) as equity contributions, with the investment amount accounting for 95.84%. On November 16, 2000, Tianyuan Group Company and Tianyuan Stock Company jointly issued a "Supplementary Undertaking to the Debt Transfer Agreement" to Sanmenxia Station ICBC. Article 2 of this written undertaking stated: "In order to prevent Sanmenxia Station ICBC's creditor's rights from being affected by the restructuring of Tianyuan Group Company and to ensure the safety of Sanmenxia Station ICBC's credit assets, Tianyuan Group Company further guarantees the repayment of its debts to Sanmenxia Station ICBC with the total assets after the completion of the 100,000-ton electrolytic aluminum expansion project. If Tianyuan Group Company is truly unable to repay its debts to Sanmenxia Station ICBC, then Tianyuan Stock Company shall be responsible for the repayment."

Tiancheng Electrochemical Company underwent bankruptcy liquidation on May 12, 2007.

Sanmenxia Station ICBC filed a lawsuit with the court of first instance on August 28, 2006, requesting a judgment ordering: Tianyuan Group Company and Tianyuan Stock Company to jointly repay the principal of RMB 37,700,000 in loans and interest of RMB 3,754,860.16 (interest calculated up to July 20, 2006, with interest thereafter continuing to accrue); and ordering Tiancheng Electrochemical Company to assume joint and several liability for repayment of the above debts within the scope of its guarantee.

After trial, the court of first instance held: Sanmenxia Station ICBC claimed that Tianyuan Group Company should repay the principal of RMB 37,700,000 and interest of RMB 3,754,860.16, and provided loan contracts, loan receipts, and overdue loan collection notices. The evidence was sufficient, and this claim of Sanmenxia Station ICBC was affirmed. Regarding the promise contained in the "Supplementary Undertaking to the Debt Transfer Agreement" issued jointly by Tianyuan Stock Company and Tianyuan Group Company to Sanmenxia Station ICBC on November 16, 2000, which stated: "If Tianyuan Group Company is truly unable to repay its debts to Sanmenxia Station ICBC, then Tianyuan Stock Company shall be responsible for the repayment," this promise had the nature of a guarantee. Since the loans in this case were old loans from the year 2000 gradually evolved through multiple rounds of "repaying old loans with new loans" and were not new loans incurred in 2004, the loans that Tianyuan Stock Company promised in November 2000 to repay jointly with Tianyuan Group Company had already been repaid. Therefore, Tianyuan Stock Company should not bear guarantee liability for the loans in this case incurred in 2004. From the content of the letter of undertaking issued by Tianyuan Group Company to Sanmenxia Station ICBC on September 21, 2000, which stated: "Tianyuan Group Company will contribute its existing high-quality assets (Electrolysis No. 1 Plant, Electrolysis No. 2 Plant, power workshop, and other auxiliary workshops) as equity contributions," it could be determined that Tianyuan Group Company, with its high-quality assets, had formed Tianyuan Stock Company together with other parties. Based on the business registration materials of Tianyuan Stock Company, its main shareholder was Tianyuan Group Company, which contributed RMB 65,176,184, representing 95.84% of the total shares. Moreover, based on the asset evaluation conducted by Asia Pacific Evaluation Firm as of November 30, 1999, its net asset value was RMB 92,326,000. From this, it could be determined that Tianyuan Group Company had contributed most of its assets into Tianyuan Stock Company. Accordingly, Tianyuan Group Company should be liable for its debts to Sanmenxia Station ICBC using its assets, including its equity stake in Tianyuan Stock Company. Since the loans in this case were old loans from the year 2000 gradually evolved through multiple rounds of "repaying old loans with new loans," Sanmenxia Station ICBC could not adduce evidence to prove that the guarantor Tiancheng Electrochemical Company knew of or consented to the practice of repaying old loans with new loans, nor could it prove that the guarantor of the old loans was also Tiancheng Electrochemical Company. Pursuant to Article 39(1) of the Supreme People's Court's Interpretation on Several Issues Concerning the Application of the Guarantee Law of the People's Republic of China, which provides: "Where the parties to the principal contract agree to repay an old loan with a new loan, the guarantor shall not bear civil liability unless the guarantor knew or should have known thereof," Tiancheng Electrochemical Company shall not bear guarantee liability for the loans in this case.

In accordance with Articles 205 and 206 of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China, Article 24 of the Guarantee Law of the People's Republic of China, Article 39(1) of the Supreme People's Court's Interpretation on Several Issues Concerning the Application of the Guarantee Law of the People's Republic of China, and Articles 130, 134, 138, 147, and 232 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the court of first instance rendered the following judgment: 1. Tianyuan Group Company shall, within ten days from the effective date of this judgment, repay to Sanmenxia Station ICBC the principal of RMB 37,700,000 and interest of RMB 3,754,860.16 (interest calculated up to July 20, 2006; interest from July 21, 2006 onward shall be calculated at the overdue loan interest rate prescribed by the People's Bank of China for the same period until the expiration of the debt performance period specified in this judgment). For the above amounts payable, if the parties fail to perform the obligation of paying monetary amounts within the period specified in this judgment, they shall, in accordance with Article 232 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, double the interest for the period of delayed performance. 2. The other claims of Sanmenxia Station ICBC are dismissed. The first-instance case acceptance fee of RMB 217,284.30 shall be borne by Tianyuan Group Company.

Sanmenxia Station ICBC, dissatisfied with the above civil judgment of the court of first instance, appealed to this Court, arguing:

1. The court of first instance already accepted Sanmenxia Station ICBC's assertion that the principal of RMB 37,700,000 in loans in this case was actually formed in 2000 and evolved from old loans in 2000 through multiple rounds of "repaying old loans with new loans," rather than being new loans incurred in 2004. However, it then determined that the loans which Tianyuan Stock Company promised in November 2000 to repay jointly with Tianyuan Group Company had already been repaid, and accordingly ruled that Tianyuan Stock Company should not bear repayment liability for the loans in this case incurred in 2004. This lacks factual basis. Tianyuan Group Company still owes Sanmenxia Station ICBC a total principal of RMB 2,308,100 in loans. None of the evidence submitted by Tianyuan Stock Company could prove that the RMB 37,700,000 in loans claimed by Sanmenxia Station Sub-branch in this case had been repaid by it or by Tianyuan Group Company. Tianyuan Stock Company should bear repayment liability in accordance with the "Supplementary Undertaking to the Debt Transfer Agreement."

2. The court of first instance found that Sanmenxia Station ICBC could not adduce evidence to prove that Tiancheng Electrochemical Company knew of or consented to the practice of repaying old loans with new loans in this case, nor could it prove that the guarantor of the old loans was also Tiancheng Electrochemical Company. Therefore, it determined that Tiancheng Electrochemical Company should not bear guarantee liability for the loans in this case. This finding violates the allocation rule of burden of proof that "he who asserts must prove." The burden of proving whether the fact of repaying old loans with new loans was known and whether the guarantors of the prior and subsequent loans were the same should be borne by Tiancheng Electrochemical Company. As the guarantor, Tiancheng Electrochemical Company failed to adduce evidence to prove the above facts and should therefore bear joint and several liability for repayment of the loans in this case. Sanmenxia Station ICBC requested that the judgment be modified on appeal to order Tianyuan Stock Company to assume joint and several liability for repayment of the principal of RMB 37,700,000 and the interest owed by Tianyuan Group Company; and to order Tiancheng Electrochemical Company to assume joint and several guarantee liability for the above principal and interest.

During the second-instance proceedings of this Court, Sanmenxia Station ICBC stated: Given that Tiancheng Electrochemical Company was adjudicated bankrupt and concluded by the People's Court of Shanxian County, Henan Province on January 22, 2008, it applied to withdraw its appeal request against Tiancheng Electrochemical Company.

The Appellee, Tianyuan Stock Company, responded: 1. In July 2000, Tianyuan Group Company, together with five other legal persons, initiated the establishment of Tianyuan Stock Company. Tianyuan Group Company contributed assets valued at over RMB 300 million after evaluation as equity into Tianyuan Stock Company. To pass the qualification certification for listing, on September 21, 2000, Tianyuan Group Company issued a "Letter of Undertaking" to Sanmenxia Station ICBC, stating that the equipment assets it contributed to Tianyuan Stock Company would only be responsible for debts of RMB 25,500,000 owed to the bank, and the remaining debts would still be borne by Tianyuan Group Company. Sanmenxia Station ICBC accepted this. Tianyuan Group Company, Tianyuan Stock Company, and Sanmenxia Station ICBC signed five "Debt Transfer Agreements" involving a total amount of RMB 25,500,000. The "Supplementary Undertaking to the Debt Transfer Agreement" issued by Tianyuan Stock Company on November 16, 2000, was based on the indivisibility of the equity property Tianyuan Stock Company received from Tianyuan Group Company, and was a commitment made specifically with respect to the RMB 25,500,000 debt owed to Sanmenxia Station ICBC that was collateralized. It did not constitute a promise to be liable for other loans between Sanmenxia Station ICBC and Tianyuan Group Company after November 2000. Tianyuan Stock Company should not bear civil liability for the loans taken out by Tianyuan Group Company with Sanmenxia Station ICBC and guarantor Tiancheng Electrochemical Company in August 2004 involved in this case. To fulfill the said "Supplementary Undertaking to the Debt Transfer Agreement," Tianyuan Stock Company entered into three "Loan Contracts" with Sanmenxia Station ICBC on September 14, 2001, each for a total of RMB 25,500,000, with the purpose stated as "to support the enterprise's listing and transfer loans." The RMB 25,500,000 loan was fully repaid on September 25 and 26, 2001. This shows that the "Supplementary Undertaking to the Debt Transfer Agreement" had been actually performed, and the rights and obligations between the parties had been discharged. 2. The three loans involved in this case were a new lending relationship that occurred in August 2004 between Tianyuan Group Company and Sanmenxia Station ICBC and guarantor Tiancheng Electrochemical Company for the purchase of raw materials for production. Tianyuan Stock Company is not a party to this lending relationship and has no direct legal connection. There is no factual or legal basis for it to assume joint repayment liability with Tianyuan Group Company. The court of first instance correctly found the facts and applied the law, and Tianyuan Stock Company requests that the second-instance court affirm the judgment.

The Defendant at First Instance, Tianyuan Group Company, was lawfully summoned by this Court but did not appear to participate in the second-instance proceedings.

In addition to confirming the facts found by the court of first instance, this Court also finds the following facts upon second-instance trial:

On September 21, 2000, Tianyuan Group Company issued a Letter of Commitment to Sanmenxia Station ICBC, bearing the company's official seal and the signature of its chairman, Li Yongzheng. The letter stated: "In order to strive for the listing of the enterprise and seek greater development, the company underwent restructuring in July 2000. Upon approval by the Henan Provincial Commission for Economic Restructuring, Tianyuan Co., Ltd. was established. Tianyuan Group Company contributed its existing high-quality assets (Electrolysis No. 1 Plant, Electrolysis No. 2 Plant, Power Workshop and other auxiliary workshops) as shares, with the total investment accounting for 95.84% of the total share capital of the Co., Ltd. At the same time, to pass the qualification certification for a listed company, it was determined that the majority of liabilities that should have been borne by the Co., Ltd. would remain with the Group Company, and the Co., Ltd. would only assume bank debts of RMB 82.32 million (including RMB 25.5 million owed to your bank). The remaining debt of RMB 108.7 million out of the RMB 134.2 million originally loaned to our Group Company by your bank would still be borne by the Group Company. To ensure that your bank's credit assets of RMB 108.7 million do not suffer losses due to our company's restructuring, and to ensure normal repayment of principal and interest on this loan, our Group solemnly commits that, for this debt of RMB 108.7 million, our Group Company will use the total assets of the Phase I 100,000-ton electrolytic aluminum expansion project (31,000 tons) upon completion as a guarantee for repaying your bank's debt. If these assets are subsequently required to enter the Co., Ltd., your bank's creditor's rights will be transferred simultaneously with such assets." Sanmenxia Station ICBC raised no objection to the authenticity of this Letter of Commitment but stated that it had never accepted it and did not agree to the request that Tianyuan Co., Ltd. only assume RMB 25.5 million of the RMB 134.2 million debt owed by Tianyuan Group Company.

Tianyuan Group Company and Tianyuan Co., Ltd. executed five Debt Transfer Agreements concerning the aforementioned RMB 25.5 million loan from Sanmenxia Station ICBC. The "Bank Credit Department Seal" section of these five agreements was not stamped with the official seal of Sanmenxia Station ICBC.

On November 16, 2000, Tianyuan Group Company and Tianyuan Co., Ltd. issued a Supplemental Commitment to the Debt Transfer Agreements to Sanmenxia Station ICBC. Article 1 of this Supplemental Commitment stated: "The Debt Transfer Agreements No. 001, 002, 003, 004, and 005 signed among Sanmenxia Station ICBC, Tianyuan Group Company, and Tianyuan Co., Ltd. were solely for the purpose of supporting the company's listing and shall not serve as substantive basis for the debt transfer and are unrelated to the Station ICBC's creditor's rights. The Group Company and the Co., Ltd. shall jointly be responsible for the Station ICBC's creditor's rights." Article 3 stated: "If the assets of the completed 100,000-ton electrolytic aluminum project are subsequently required to enter the Co., Ltd., the Station ICBC's creditor's rights shall be transferred simultaneously with such assets."

According to the announcement titled "Very Substantial Acquisition and Connected Transaction" published by Tianyuan Co., Ltd. on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange on October 27, 2005, Tianyuan Group Company had leased the 31,000-ton electrolytic aluminum equipment of Tianyuan Co., Ltd. since June 13, 2004. On the announcement date, the parties entered into an agreement whereby Tianyuan Co., Ltd. acquired the 31,000-ton electrolytic aluminum production line and auxiliary facilities of Tianyuan Group Company, as well as part of the land use rights of Tianyuan Group Company, at a consideration of RMB 390.78 million, through assuming Tianyuan Group Company's debts owed to financial institutions (excluding Station ICBC), accounts receivable, procurement deposits, and cash payments. The 31,000-ton electrolytic aluminum production line and auxiliary facilities were valued at RMB 314.96 million.

Tianyuan Group Company had transferred all its equity interests in Tianyuan Co., Ltd. (accounting for 67.2% of the total share capital of Tianyuan Co., Ltd.) to a third party, Tianrui Company.

On May 25, 2007, the People's Court of Shanxian County, Henan Province, ruled to bankrupt and liquidate Tiancheng Electrochemical Company. On January 22, 2008, the same court ruled to conclude the bankruptcy case, with unsecured claims no longer to be satisfied. According to the bankruptcy administrator's distribution plan, the recovery ratio for ordinary unsecured creditors in that case was zero.

This Court is of the opinion that: Tianyuan Group Company failed to repay the principal of RMB 37.7 million and interest on the loan from Sanmenxia Station ICBC as agreed, constituting a breach of contract. All parties to this case have no objection to this fact. Therefore, this Court affirms the part of the original judgment concerning Tianyuan Group Company's civil liability. The focus of the second instance is: whether Tianyuan Co., Ltd. should bear joint repayment liability for Tianyuan Group Company's debt in this case.

(1) Article 84 of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China provides: "Where a debtor transfers all or part of its obligations under a contract to a third party, it shall obtain the consent of the creditor." Tianyuan Group Company, by contributing its high-quality assets to establish Tianyuan Co., Ltd. with others, invested net assets of RMB 92.326 million into Tianyuan Co., Ltd., thereby reducing its property available for repaying bank debts and weakening its debt repayment capacity. During the restructuring process, Tianyuan Group Company issued the Letter of Commitment to Sanmenxia Station ICBC, proposing that the equipment assets it invested in Tianyuan Co., Ltd. would only be responsible for RMB 25.5 million of the total RMB 134.2 million debt owed to that bank, with the remaining debt still to be borne by Tianyuan Group Company. Sanmenxia Station ICBC did not accept this commitment and also did not affix its official seal to the five Debt Transfer Agreements signed between Tianyuan Group Company and Tianyuan Co., Ltd. concerning the RMB 25.5 million loan. Therefore, these debt transfer agreements did not take legal effect with respect to Sanmenxia Station ICBC.

(2) The Supplemental Commitment to the Debt Transfer Agreements signed by Tianyuan Group Company and Tianyuan Co., Ltd. on November 16, 2000, actually made the following three promises to Sanmenxia Station ICBC: First, the aforementioned debt transfer agreements signed by Tianyuan Group Company and Tianyuan Co., Ltd. were made only for the needs of the company's listing and were not substantive basis for debt transfer. That is, the two parties had negated the legal effect of the five debt transfer agreements and promised that Tianyuan Group Company and Tianyuan Co., Ltd. would jointly be responsible for Sanmenxia Station ICBC's creditor's rights. Second, Tianyuan Group Company would use the total assets of the completed 100,000-ton electrolytic aluminum expansion project as a guarantee for repaying the debt to Sanmenxia Station ICBC. If Tianyuan Group Company was unable to repay the debt to Sanmenxia Station ICBC, the debt would be repaid by Tianyuan Co., Ltd. Third, if the assets of the completed 100,000-ton electrolytic aluminum project were subsequently required to enter the Co., Ltd., Sanmenxia Station ICBC's creditor's rights would be transferred simultaneously with such assets. The meaning of this commitment is clear. Article 1 constitutes a concurrent assumption of debt, i.e., joinder of the debtor. Tianyuan Group Company is not released from its original debt obligation; Tianyuan Co., Ltd. joins Tianyuan Group Company's debt obligation to Sanmenxia Station ICBC, promising to jointly bear the repayment responsibility with Tianyuan Group Company. Article 2 constitutes a guarantee for the debt, i.e., Tianyuan Group Company uses the 100,000-ton electrolytic aluminum assets as repayment guarantee, and in the event of its inability to repay the debt, Tianyuan Co., Ltd. assumes the guarantee liability. Article 3 actually constitutes a conditional assumption of debt with release, with the condition being that the 100,000-ton electrolytic aluminum assets enter Tianyuan Co., Ltd. When this condition is fulfilled, Tianyuan Group Company is released from its original debt obligation, and Tianyuan Co., Ltd. directly assumes the repayment responsibility to Sanmenxia Station ICBC. Sanmenxia Station ICBC recognized the Supplemental Commitment. Based on the facts that, of the 100,000-ton electrolytic aluminum assets, 69,000 tons of assets entered Tianyuan Co., Ltd. upon its establishment, and the remaining 31,000 tons of assets were leased by Tianyuan Co., Ltd. from June 13, 2004, and were acquired on October 27, 2005, by assuming Tianyuan Group Company's debts and paying partial cash, Sanmenxia Station ICBC believed that the condition attached in the Supplemental Commitment had been fulfilled. This Court supports its appeal request that Tianyuan Co., Ltd. should bear the repayment liability for Tianyuan Group Company's debt in this case. At the same time, Tianyuan Group Company's repayment liability could have been exempted, but since it did not appeal this point, and combined with the promise in Article 1 of the Supplemental Commitment, Tianyuan Co., Ltd. and Tianyuan Group Company shall bear joint repayment liability for the principal and interest of RMB 37.7 million in this case.

(3) Regarding Tianyuan Co., Ltd.'s argument that the three loans in question in this case were new loan relationships that arose in August 2004 between Tianyuan Group Company, due to production needs for purchasing raw materials, and Sanmenxia Station ICBC and the guarantor Tiancheng Electrochemical Company, and that Tianyuan Co., Ltd. is not a party to these loan relationships and should not bear civil liability. This Court is of the opinion that, based on the facts ascertained in this case, from the loan purposes stipulated in the contracts and the operational methods of lending and repayment, it can be determined that the three loans of Tianyuan Group Company sued by Sanmenxia Station ICBC in this case, i.e., Loan Contracts (2004) No. 37, No. 38, and No. 39, are all loan contracts for repaying old loans with new loans. Loan Contract (2004) No. 37 for RMB 15.9 million is a repayment of a loan for an old loan of RMB 17 million existing before 2000, after several rounds of rolling over. Loan Contract (2004) No. 38 for RMB 14.8 million and Loan Contract No. 39 for RMB 7 million are repayments of a loan for an old loan contract of RMB 16.47 million existing before 2000, after several rounds of rolling over. The original judgment correctly found that the loans in this case evolved gradually from old loans in 2000 through multiple rounds of lending to repay existing loans. Loan-for-old-loan is a practice where, when a loan is due and cannot be recovered on time, a financial institution issues a new loan to the original borrower to repay the original loan. This practice is fundamentally different from a borrower using its own funds to repay a loan, thereby extinguishing the original creditor-debtor relationship. Although the new loan replaces the old loan, the creditor-debtor relationship between the lender and the borrower is not eliminated; objectively, it merely extends the repayment period of the old loan in the form of a new loan. Therefore, a loan-for-old-loan is essentially a special form of extension of the old loan. In this case, the related old loans of Tianyuan Group Company were not actually repaid. Therefore, Tianyuan Co., Ltd. shall still bear civil liability for the above three loans of Tianyuan Group Company in accordance with its commitment.

(4) In this second instance, Tianyuan Co., Ltd. argued that the Supplemental Commitment in this case was a commitment issued to Sanmenxia Station ICBC regarding the RMB 25.5 million debt of Tianyuan Group Company that Tianyuan Co., Ltd. had agreed to assume, and did not constitute a commitment to bear responsibility for other borrowings between Sanmenxia Station ICBC and Tianyuan Group Company. To perform the aforementioned Supplemental Commitment, Tianyuan Co., Ltd. signed three loan contracts with Sanmenxia Station ICBC on September 14, 2001, to transfer loans of RMB 25.5 million, and these RMB 25.5 million loans had been fully repaid. The Supplemental Commitment had been actually performed, and the rights and obligations between the parties had been terminated. Regarding this, this Court is of the opinion that the Supplemental Commitment did not explicitly stipulate that Tianyuan Co., Ltd. would only bear civil liability to Sanmenxia Station ICBC for Tianyuan Group Company's RMB 25.5 million debt. Tianyuan Co., Ltd. submitted three repayment vouchers to this Court in the second instance, proving that on September 25, 2000, September 26, 2000, and September 26, 2000, it repaid RMB 25.5 million to Sanmenxia Station ICBC on behalf of Tianyuan Group Company under the name of loan transfer. Sanmenxia Station ICBC did not deny this, and both parties agreed that these repayments were not repayments of the debt in this case. Therefore, this Court confirms this fact. However, all three repayments occurred before November 16, 2000, when Tianyuan Co., Ltd. issued the Supplemental Commitment to Sanmenxia Station ICBC. It is difficult to conclude that these repayments were made to perform the Supplemental Commitment. Therefore, this Court does not support Tianyuan Co., Ltd.'s claim that Sanmenxia Station ICBC had actually tacitly approved Tianyuan Co., Ltd.'s undertaking only RMB 25.5 million of Tianyuan Group Company's debt, and that the agreement had been terminated through performance.

(5) Regarding the issue of the legal status and civil liability of Tiancheng Electrochemical Company. Given that before the hearing of this Court in the second instance, Tiancheng Electrochemical Company was ruled bankrupt and its proceedings concluded by the People's Court of Shanxian County, Henan Province on January 22, 2008, its legal status as a civil subject ceased to exist upon the conclusion of the bankruptcy proceedings. Therefore, Tiancheng Electrochemical Company can no longer be a party to this case.

In summary, the original judgment failed to clearly ascertain some facts and improperly determined liability. In accordance with Article 153, Paragraph 1, Subparagraph (3) of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, this Court hereby renders the following judgment:

1. Affirm Item 2 of the Civil Judgment (2006) Yu Fa Min Er Chu Zi No. 44 of the Henan Higher People's Court;

2. Amend Item 1 of the main text of the aforementioned civil judgment to read: Sanmenxia Tianyuan Aluminum Industry Group Co., Ltd. and Sanmenxia Tianyuan Aluminum Industry Co., Ltd. shall, within ten days after this judgment takes effect, repay to China Industrial and Commercial Bank Co., Ltd., Sanmenxia Station Branch, the loan principal of RMB 37.7 million and interest of RMB 3,754,860.16 (calculated up to July 20, 2006; from July 21, 2006 onwards, interest shall be calculated and paid in installments according to the overdue loan interest rate for the corresponding period prescribed by the People's Bank of China until the date of full payment). If the obligors mentioned above fail to perform the payment obligation within the period specified in this judgment, they shall, in accordance with Article 232 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, pay double the interest on the debt for the period of delayed performance.

The first-instance court acceptance fee of RMB 217,284.3 shall be jointly borne by Sanmenxia Tianyuan Aluminum Industry Group Co., Ltd. and Sanmenxia Tianyuan Aluminum Industry Co., Ltd.; the second-instance court acceptance fee of RMB 217,284.3 shall be jointly borne by Sanmenxia Tianyuan Aluminum Industry Group Co., Ltd. and Sanmenxia Tianyuan Aluminum Industry Co., Ltd.

This judgment is final.
